## Introduction

The data come from [TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/blob/main/README.md). TidyTuestday is a weekly social data project for the R community. Read more about TidyTuesday [here](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday) and see people's contributions on Twitter under the [#TidyTuesday hashtag](https://x.com/hashtag/TidyTuesday?src=hashtag_click&f=live)

## Data overview

Let's load the libraries and import the data first.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| warning: FALSE
#| message: FALSE

library(tidyverse)
library(skimr)
```

```{r}
#| label: data-import
#| warning: FALSE
#| message: FALSE

members       <- read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2020/2020-09-22/members.csv')
expeditions   <- read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2020/2020-09-22/expeditions.csv')
peaks         <- read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2020/2020-09-22/peaks.csv')
```

### Members

```{r skim-members}
skim(members)
```

## Peaks

```{r skim-peaks}
skim(peaks)
```

## Popular peaks

```{r expeditions per peaks}
expeditions %>% 
  count(peak_name, sort = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(proportion = n / sum(n))
```

```{r members per peaks}
members %>% 
  count(peak_name, name = 'member_count') %>%
  arrange(desc(member_count)) %>%
  mutate(proportion = member_count / sum(member_count))
```

## Hired and died

```{r hired and died}
members %>%
  group_by(hired) %>%
  count(hired, died) %>%
  mutate(proportion = n/ sum(n))
```

```{r}
ggplot(members, aes(y = hired, fill = died)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill")
```
